hypothesis: The neuron responds primarily to prominent vertical lines, edges, or elongated structures that bisect the visual field or create a sharp boundary between contrasting regions. These features include physical objects like poles, pens, rods, and stems, as well as structural boundaries such as door edges, seams, gaps between objects, or the sides of signs. The neuron is invariant to object identity, material, and background context, provided the vertical orientation and structural linearity are maintained. The activating vertical feature typically spans 80–100% of the image height and is positioned centrally or slightly off-center, often occupying a narrow width (5–10% of the frame) or serving as a divider between two larger distinct areas. The visual pattern relies on strong contrast; the vertical element is often dark (black, dark brown, deep grey) or metallic, set against a background or adjacent region of a differing, often lighter, tone such as beige, white, sky blue, or green.
